A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowMo research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet-1K reconstruction and generation experiments, architectural and training ablations, and a rate-distortion-perception analysis.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds dataset and resolution generalization, scaling, post-training diagnostics, and runtime measurements in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces use of a patchwise diffuse-and-blend inference strategy for higher-resolution reconstruction, an adaptation absent from v1. The transformer/LFQ architecture, two-stage training scheme, and shifted sampler remain unchanged. The added Flux attribution and conditioning-dropout description do not establish changes to the original implementation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates reconstruction and generation on ImageNet-1K at 256×256. v3 adds reconstruction on OpenImages and Food-101, plus 512×512 evaluation on all three datasets (Table 8). This substantially broadens evaluation to unseen datasets and resolutions while retaining ImageNet-only tokenizer training.

E2.justification: The corresponding tokenization, generation, and DiTo comparisons retain their comparator memberships in Tables 1–3. The added generalization and timing evaluations reuse Cosmos DI-8x8 and LlamaGen-32. Newly discussed works such as epsilon-VAE and DiscoDiff are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: v3 revises reported FlowMo-Lo pre-training from 100 to 130 epochs and changes Table 6's entropy and commitment weights from 0.1 to 0.0025 and 0.0025 to 0.000625. It also adds a controlled 200K-step width sweep and reconstruction precision/recall evaluation against separate training and validation references. These substantially expand and revise reported settings; they do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2–C.6 adds generalization tests, width-scaling analysis, precision/recall diagnostics of mode seeking, post-training ablations for smaller and continuous-latent models, and runtime comparisons. Existing ablations and the rate-distortion-perception study remain. The brief v1 finding that varying latent sequence length produced no significant benefit is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report quantitative results as point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reconstruction variance visualization in Figure 8 is retained; the new experiments introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–5 and 7 remain unchanged, but Appendix C adds substantial numerical evidence. New findings include scaling rFID from 7.77 to 3.84 across tested widths and smaller-model post-training rFID from 2.02 to 1.21. Table 8's row labeled FlowMo-Hi beats Cosmos in five conditions but loses on Food-101 at 256 resolution, 1.39 versus 1.05. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1's retained scores.

T1.justification: Equation 11 changes the sampling-chain input from data x to noise z, correcting the mathematical definition of the post-training loss to agree with the already-existing Figure 5. v3 also removes the assertion that the rectified-flow objective becomes singular at t=0. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain state-of-the-art ImageNet tokenization at the two compression rates through transformer-based diffusion autoencoding and mode-seeking post-training, without adversarial losses or auxiliary-tokenizer distillation. The qualified claim about downstream generation is retained. Shortening the conclusion does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: C.4 adds an interpretation of why post-training improves both precision and recall against matched validation images but trades recall for precision against training-set statistics. C.6 distinguishes encoding cost from decoding cost, argues encoding does not bottleneck second-stage training, and suggests possible distillation speedups. These refine v1's mechanism discussion and existing inference-time limitation.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies Flux as an implementation source and specifies 10% latent-conditioning dropout without class conditioning; v1 already used classifier-free guidance. It revises hyperparameters, adds per-image timings, and changes the abstract from promising a release to reporting code and model availability. The explicit token-factorization '(9, 9) split' statement is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for epsilon-VAE and DiscoDiff, credits Flux, and removes the SiT and Consistency Models references. The main positioning relative to diffusion autoencoders, TiTok, DiTo, and FlexTok remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order remain intact. Appendix C becomes 'Additional Experiments,' with the original tradeoff discussion retained as C.1 and new subsections C.2–C.6. There are localized explanatory additions, a shortened conclusion, and an acknowledgment, rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 8 and four compact, unnumbered appendix tables. Figure 9 moves above the new analyses, the extended visualization pages shift later, and Table 7's caption is clarified. All thirteen existing figures retain their content, and the overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: v3 usefully strengthens v1's ImageNet-focused evidence with generalization tests, scaling and post-training diagnostics, and numerical runtime comparisons. The Equation 11 correction and added implementation details also improve clarity. These are incremental gains: central results remain unchanged, while C.2's FlowMo-Lo prose conflicts with Table 8's FlowMo-Hi label, and the new generalization and timing protocols lack sufficient detail for precise reproduction.
